title: Carlos Alcaraz defeats Alexander Zverev to win ATP Finals
seoTitle: Alcaraz beats Zverev to win ATP Finals
dek: Carlos Alcaraz defeated Alexander Zverev in straight sets in Turin to claim his first ATP Finals title.
happened: According to reports from Turin, Carlos Alcaraz faced world number one Alexander Zverev in the championship match of the ATP Finals on 22 November. Alcaraz secured a 6-2, 7-6 victory in just over two hours, capturing the season-ending tournament for the first time. The 23-year-old Spaniard dominated the opening set by breaking his opponent three times. Although the second set proved more competitive with Zverev fighting back to level at 4-4 and holding multiple set points in the tie-break, Alcaraz clinched the victory on his second match point with a backhand winner. With this triumph, Alcaraz earned a record $5.2 million prize and joined Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic as the only men to win all four major titles and the ATP Finals. Alcaraz finished the year with 14 consecutive victories, having also won titles at the Vienna Open and Paris Masters.

sides.says: Reflecting on his victory, Alcaraz stated, "This trophy is something I have been chasing for a really long time. It means the world to me." He added, "It’s a privilege, and I’m just really proud."
The top-seeded German reached the final after winning both the French Open and US Open earlier in the year, finishing his season as the world number one.

next: Carlos Alcaraz plans to join Spain's Davis Cup team in Bologna, Italy, where they are scheduled to face Team Austria in the quarterfinals on 26 November.
summary: Carlos Alcaraz defeated Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6 in Turin on 22 November to win his first ATP Finals title. The victory made the 23-year-old Spaniard just the fourth man in tennis history to win all four Grand Slam titles and the season-ending tournament, joining an elite group containing Roger Federer, Andre Agassi and Novak Djokovic. Alcaraz completed the tournament undefeated despite battling leg and hamstring issues, collecting a record $5.2 million prize and extending his winning streak to 14 matches.
